title: The Token Arcade
clue: Five tokens, a very small counter and a ticket price nobody expected.
reveal: Open a tiny arcade for a lively dog. Each booth is a short game your dog picks by choosing a toy, and every ticket is paid in your stillness, not theirs: ten slow breaths at the counter and the next booth opens. The last booth is the quietest.
objective: Run four short booths your dog chooses, pay for each with ten slow breaths, and close the arcade on a read-aloud.
instructions: Build the arcade in a clear room, hallway or checked, fenced yard with grippy footing (rugs, a yoga mat). Put a mat with a water bowl in one corner: that is the counter. Put a jar on a table or shelf beside the mat, out of paw reach, with five tokens in it: large wooden spoons or chunky jar lids, too big for your dog to swallow. Nothing breakable, no stairs.

Set four booths on the floor, each a towel (a paper sign is optional): Roll (a soft ball bigger than your dog's mouth, rolled along a clear stretch), Find (a toy under a folded towel in plain view), Tunnel (a sheet over two chairs, open at both ends, with a toy visible at the far end), Parade (a plush toy to carry to the counter, if your dog likes carrying). Match each booth to a toy so the toy can pick the game.

Open the arcade: sit on the counter mat and hold out two of the booth toys, low and still. Whichever your dog leans toward is the first booth. Walk with them to that booth and play for a minute or two, with no more than three rolls, finds or runs. Stop while they are still keen.

Pay at the counter: sit on the mat, hands in your lap, and take ten slow breaths while you move one token from the jar to a tray beside it. This is your price, not theirs: your dog can drink, lie down, sniff, wander or stay bouncy. If they are still wound up, the price goes up by ten breaths (inflation). The next booth opens only when they look ready, and the arcade may close at any time.
Play the second and third booths the same way, again letting the toys choose. Between booths keep your voice low and slow. Skip any booth your dog ignores: tokens do not have to be spent.

Prize counter, the surprise: fetch a toy your dog has not seen for a week from a cupboard, wrapped in a towel on the counter mat. Unwrap it with a flourish and let them have the first sniff and a gentle play. Put today's other toys away so nothing is competing.

Last booth, the Quiet Booth: dim the lights, sit on the counter mat and read a page or two aloud in a low voice. Your dog can settle beside you, in their bed or somewhere else. If they wander off, finish your page anyway.

Cash out: tear a scrap-paper ticket stub for each booth you visited. Unspent tokens stay in the jar, because the best score is the most left over. Put the jar back up on the shelf and return the prize toy to its cupboard for next time.
twist: Nobody earns anything by being good. You pay every ticket in stillness, your dog's toy choice picks each booth, and the best score is tokens left over.
variations: Small apartment or a short session: three booths in one room, any three of the four, and one token left in the jar.
Seated owner: roll, find and parade from a chair, with the booths within arm's reach and the counter beside you.
Gentle or older dog: only the Find booth and the Quiet Booth, played slowly on a rug. Ask your vet what suits them.
Fenced yard circuit: four towels as booths on dry, level ground you have walked first, with water at the counter and a shaded spot. Skip it in heat, frost or cold.
completion: Counts after any booth and a quiet pay-at-the-counter, even if your dog skips most of the arcade or the prize stays wrapped.
photoIdea: The strip of ticket stubs next to the jar of unspent tokens, with a sleepy dog or a toy in the corner of the frame.
memoryPrompt: Which toy chose the first booth, and what did your dog do while you paid for it?
supplies: A mat and a water bowl
A jar and five large wooden spoons or chunky jar lids, too big to swallow
A soft ball bigger than your dog's mouth
Two or three of your dog's toys
optionalSupplies: A book or magazine for the Quiet Booth
substitutes: No jar? A mixing bowl on a table or shelf works.
No sheet and chairs? A large cardboard box on its side, open at both ends, is the tunnel.
safety: Use a non-slip floor and a clear room. Keep each booth to a minute or two, max three repeats, and no chasing, zoomies or tug.
Tokens, balls and toys must be intact and too big to swallow; the jar stays off the floor. The tunnel stays open at both ends.
A game, not a calming exercise: if your dog will not settle, close the arcade. Puppies get two booths and lots of rest.

teaser: The booths are open and the prizes are priceless.
